title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

errors: The equivalence (i) <=> (ii) uses monotonicity of i ↦ X_i. The marginal note proposes dropping 'i<=j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j'. Without it, (i) does not imply (ii). Counterexample: I = {0<1}, X_0 = {a}, X_1 = {b}. Each I^x has a least element, yet X_1 ∩ X_1 = {b} ≠ X_0 ∪ X_1. The (i)-(iii) equivalence also needs care, because (ii) with i=j forces monotonicity. So the marginal generalisation needs an extra hypothesis.

'Automatic if I finite' for b) and for existence of minimal elements only needs every I^x (or I_{<=i}) to be well-founded; finiteness is sufficient but stronger than needed. This is minor and not an error.
Otherwise the statements check out. (ii) ⇒ (i): if m is minimal in I^x and i ∈ I^x, then x ∈ X_i ∩ X_m = ∪_{k<=i,m} X_k, which forces m <= i. (iv)(γ) follows from j = min I^x for any x ∈ X_j°.

ideas.what: An increasing poset-indexed family of subsets defines a stratification (x ↦ min I^x) iff each I^x has a least element; equivalent formulations via disjoint open strata, closed strata as unions of open strata, and intersection = union over common lower bounds
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified set / map to a poset with Alexandrov topology; closed strata X_{<=p} = s^{-1}(P_{<=p}); face-poset combinatorics of cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore. Stratifications over posets appear in Goresky–MacPherson-era work and later formalisations (e.g. Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka); face posets of regular CW complexes are standard (e.g. Björner).
ideas.where_published: Unsure. The Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratified structures in general terms, but not this lemma.

ideas.what: Boundary ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j and open stratum X_i° = X_i \ ∂X_i defined purely combinatorially from the index order, with x ∈ X_i° iff i is minimal in I^x
ideas.modern_name: Strata as fibres of the stratification map; 'open cells' of a closure-finite decomposition

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct order-theoretic bookkeeping: characterising when a poset-indexed family of closed pieces comes from a stratification map. It is useful scaffolding for Grothendieck's tame-topology/cell-complex programme but is standard folklore today. The only notable detail is the marginal wish to drop monotonicity, which would actually break (i) ⇒ (ii).
transcription_corrections: In '(automat. si I fini)' under (ii), the insertion sits between 'tout x ∈ |Φ|' and 'élément minimal'. It is written above the line and qualifies the existence of a minimal element.

The phrase 'un ensemble c-ordonné[?] des loc. cit' is uncertain in the image. It possibly reads 'C-complet[?]' or similar, and the parenthetical begins earlier (an opening parenthesis is missing in the transcription).
In (iii) a), '∀ (i,j) ∈ I' should be '∀ (i,j) ∈ I×I' or '∀ i,j ∈ I' (likely a slip in the original).
